subject: Provisional SLO flexibility request — alpha model pilot integration
messages:
From: Raquel Diaz <raquel@heightshealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alpha model pilot - SLO question

Hi Grace,

Quick question ahead of our integration cutover next week. We are planning to put the alpha LLM (encoder-2a) into our staging traffic mix for a week-long pilot. Our infra team is concerned the new model's 99p latency and burst behavior might cause downstream timeouts in our ingestion pipeline.

Can Redwood provide a short-term concession on latency SLOs for the pilot window, or recommend configuration that would let us proceed without a full production SLA change? From our POV a bounded, documented temporary variance would be acceptable if there are failback controls and visibility.

Also need to know whether we can route a percentage of traffic to the stable v1 model automatically if the alpha model breaches a threshold.

Thanks — happy to hop on an hour call if easier.

—Raquel
Raquel Diaz
Director, Integrations
Heights Health
raquel@heightshealth.com

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Raquel Diaz <raquel@heightshealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional SLO flexibility request — alpha model pilot integration

Hi Raquel —

Thanks for the heads up and the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can support a bounded, documented flexibility plan for a time-limited pilot, provided we pair it with strict routing and telemetry guardrails. Below is a proposed approach we can commit to operationally for the 4-week pilot window:

- Temporary latency allowance: relax 99th-percentile latency SLO from 250ms -> 400ms for requests routed to the alpha model, active only for pilot traffic and only in the US region.
- Automatic fallback: configure smart routing to divert traffic to the stable v1 model when rolling 5-minute 99p latency > 450ms or error rate > 1.5%.
- Visibility: weekly executive dashboard + daily incident log to your SRE lead; token-level latency/queue-depth breakdowns enabled.
- Mitigations: prefix/KV caching enabled, suggested batching limits attached (see alpha_pilot_traffic_plan.pdf).
- Duration & rollback: agreement valid for 4 weeks from pilot start; immediate rollback to baseline SLO on request from either party.

If acceptable I will loop in Lauren for the commercial acknowledgement and Marcus on runbook/fallback wiring. I attached a brief traffic plan; Marcus will attach the mitigation runbook.

If you want this documented as a short amendment we can share a DocuSign link for signature.

Best,
Grace Occonnor
Sr. Manager, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0191

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Raquel Diaz <raquel@heightshealth.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional SLO flexibility request — alpha model pilot integration

Thanks Grace. Adding a few technical clarifications for the runbook and what we'll instrument: 

- Routing: we'll create a route policy that pins a pilot subset (by API key + header) to alpha-2a. The policy includes a circuit-breaker that trips to stable v1 when 5-min rolling 99p latency exceeds 450ms OR error rate spikes > 1.5%. Re-enable after 10 minutes of healthy metrics.
- Telemetry: we will export per-route 50/95/99 latencies, QPS, inflight tokens and model queue length to your Datadog account via the existing integration (will need a short-lived API key).
- KV/prefix cache: recommend enabling prefix cache TTL=60s for the pilot; this reduces tail latency for repeated prompts.
- Load shaping: see attached mitigation_runbook.md for a soft-throttle preemptive policy (we'll gate bursts over 20 RPS per API key to alpha).
- Safety net: maintain a manual escalation channel to our oncall and a weekly rollout sync.

I'll be responsible for deploying the routing policy and wiring telemetry. If you want, we can test the fallback policy in our staging environment today.

—Marcus Lin
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Raquel Diaz <raquel@heightshealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional SLO flexibility request — alpha model pilot integration

Thanks Grace and Marcus — this reads well and addresses our operational concerns. Two follow-ups from procurement: 

1) We need a short (1-paragraph) contractual acknowledgment that the change is temporary and limited to the pilot (dates + metrics threshold) and that credits for SLA breaches during the pilot are capped.
2) Can Redwood offer a modest service credit as a gesture if the alpha route causes downstream retries or incidents? Our legal prefers explicit numeric language to avoid ambiguity.

If you can draft a short amendment we can route it internally for sign-off. We are ready to begin the pilot on Monday 2026-09-06 pending this.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Raquel
Director, Integrations
Heights Health

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Raquel Diaz <raquel@heightshealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional SLO flexibility request — alpha model pilot integration

Hi Raquel —

Appreciate the clarity. Redwood can provide a one-off amendment that codifies the pilot window and the temporary SLO variance. Proposed commercial terms: 

- Amendment: defines pilot dates, the temporary 99p latency target (400ms) and explicit fallback thresholds (450ms/1.5% errors).
- Credits: SLA credit limited to a maximum of 20% of that month’s usage invoiced to Heights Health for any verified downtime or performance regressions attributable to the alpha route during the pilot.
- Documentation: amendment will be a 1‑page addendum to the existing MSA; DocuSign link below for review.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/XYZ-AlphaSLO-Amendment
Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/RED-9312 (runbook + tasks)

If that works I will send the amendment for electronic signature today so you can start 2026-09-06. Marcus — please confirm the runbook link is the same RED-9312.
